sophia: Quick update — did a focused perf pass: Triton fused/paged-attn vs our CUDA fused kernels across SM80 (A100) and SM90 (H100) with CUDA 12.1 and 12.3. Short summary: SM80/CUDA12.1: Triton wins on small batches <8 for 2k seqs; SM90/CUDA12.3: our CUDA kernels are 15-30% faster in steady-state for large batches and long seqs. Full logs below.

mario: nice. Can you paste the key numbers? :eyes:

sophia: sure — pasted runs (measured tokens/sec and p99 latency ms). config: batch_size, seq_len, model = 7B FP16, 1xGPU.

```
# Triton fused_paged (CUDA12.1 / SM80)
batch=4 seq=2048 tokens/s=21000 p99=94ms mem=28GB
batch=8 seq=2048 tokens/s=38000 p99=120ms mem=30GB

# CUDA fused (CUDA12.3 / SM90)
batch=4 seq=2048 tokens/s=24000 p99=82ms mem=27GB
batch=8 seq=2048 tokens/s=47000 p99=100ms mem=29GB
```

elaine: interesting that p99 drop on SM90 with CUDA12.3. Any idea root cause?

sophia: profiler (nsys + nvprof) shows SM90 run suffers more warp divergence in the paged-scan path — shared memory bank pressure combined with Triton's automatic scheduling leads to suboptimal occupancy on H100 for the paged step. Also saw KV cache writes stall when seq_len crosses page boundary; that serializes tokens for ~2-3ms per request at 2k.

ankur: can we workaround in runtime? maybe force a different kernel when page crossing detected.

sophia: yes — proposed heuristic: if (seq_len >= 1024 && batch >= 8) prefer cuda_fused; if page_cross_rate > 0.1 prefer cuda_fused; else for small batches prefer triton_fused (lower launch overhead). Implemented a prototype switch in kernel_selector; added a lightweight sampling pass to estimate page_cross_rate per workload.

mario: did you run regression tests? any perf regressions vs main?

sophia: ran canary across internal suites: most workloads improved, but found a regression on very short-chat style (seq<128, batch=1) with cuda_fused: +12% p50 latency due to larger kernel launch overhead. Plan: keep per-route policy to fall back to triton for <128 tokens.

ci-bot: deploy-check results: kernel-selector patch landed to canary cluster, no infra failures, perf change summary uploaded to S3 (link)

elaine: next steps?

sophia: 1) tune shared memory tiling for SM90 paged stage (experimenting with 64 vs 128 byte stride), 2) add runtime telemetry for page_cross_rate and kernel_choice histograms, 3) push an A/B rollout: 10% traffic with new selector + canary metrics. I'll open a PR with benchmark scripts and perf traces.

mario: thanks. please include exact profiler commands and nsys timeline screenshot in PR. :thumbsup:

sophia: will do — attaching command snippets:

```
nsys profile -o out --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --stats true --force true -- python run_bench.py --model 7B --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kernel fused_paged
```

ankur: sounds good. ping when PR is up and mark for eng-runtime review.

sophia: pinged in thread when PR is ready. :rocket:
